svg.text: Fig. M7 A miss through the fill buffers, the L2 and the prefetchers
The number of outstanding misses is a hole. The KB bounds it by Little's law; the fill buffer pool is the KB conjecture; the L2 indexing is measured.
Fill buffers (KB conjecture: one per 64 B line, shared)
line address | 4 x 16 B valid | waiters (load ids) | prefetch flag
Little's law from the measured L2 bandwidth: 85 GB/s at 3.2 GHz is
26.6 B/cycle; at 17 cycles that is 452 B in flight, 7.1 lines. So at
least 7 buffers (KB). A pointer chase into the L2 needs only one.
A second miss to a line in flight joins the entry; a load that finds no
free buffer replays (KB). My guess at the count: 16, since 3 loads a
cycle and prefetch make 7 too tight.

Set bits span the 16 KiB page offset (13:7) and the page frame (19:14), so the index needs the physical
address; two of the bits are XORed with higher frame bits (hashed), which is why some strides crowd a fraction of the cache.
Each 128 B line is two 64 B halves that fill and evict on their own (measured); one study sees only the touched half
go to the L1, another sees both. Ordering at the L2 is per 128 B line (patent).
Replacement: LRU among one core's lines; across cores not LRU (measured). The L2 is inclusive of the L1Ds and its
victim choice spares lines an L1D still holds (AutoLock, measured). A partial tag way filter limits which ways are read (inferred).
Four 3 MiB cachelets, one beside each core (likely in effect): one core sees 17 cycles to 3 MiB, more beyond, and
about 7.5 MiB in all. Proposed: the two hashed index bits choose the cachelet, and a line placed by core k
in another core's cachelet pays the fabric hop, which is the latency step at 3 MiB.
Arbitration (KB conjecture): per core request queues feed each L2 bank round robin, demand before prefetch.
Test (KB): three cores streaming through the L2 and a fourth pointer chasing; its latency stays flat under round robin.
L1 to L2 path 32 B/cycle each way (derived); copies cap near 150 GB/s on L1 to L2 coherence work (inferred).
Prefetchers, trained on virtual addresses in the LSU
Access map, one per region (AMPM like, inferred)
A
A
A
P
P
A accessed, P prefetched; a stride 2 pattern in the map is matched and extended (region size unknown, 4 KiB in the AMPM paper)
map granularity grows from 64 B to 128 B to 256 B for long patterns (measured, Handley v2). 16 stride streams at once (measured).
Side tables: large stride, and spatial memory streaming for dense regions (inferred).
Temporal history (inferred): a GHB like buffer of just under 256 entries covers random access inside a 15 KiB region, not 16 KiB.
Proposed: the 15 KiB bound is the 256 entry buffer minus a few entries the probe loop itself consumes; 15 KiB / 64 B = 240 lines.
Data memory dependent prefetcher (measured, Augury and GoFetch)
Pointer chasing rule
scans filled lines for 8 B values that look like pointers into the same 4 GiB region
arms after 3 accesses with a stride up to 8 KiB, reaches 64 KiB past the trained array
one dereference level; prefetches the pointed to line into the L2, not the L1
a 128 entry history filter stops repeats (derived); off only via a privileged HID11 bit
Throttle (patent): every 32 cycles the L2 rates each core's prefetch queue and sets a level; credits cap a region near
4 prefetches in flight; prefetch grows bolder when misses return late. Deny list for lines evicted unused (patent).
Non temporal loads are not prefetched into the L1 (inferred). Streaming stores become non temporal on their own (inferred).
Which level each prefetcher fills (inferred): stride and region into the L1D through the fill buffers (hence the stolen bank cycles); DMP and temporal into the L2 only.
Proposed test for the fill buffer share: a stride stream that keeps 16 lines in flight plus a pointer chase. If the chase slows, demand and prefetch share one pool.
Beyond the L2: Little's law again gives about 48 L2 lines of 128 B in flight to draw 64 GB/s from DRAM at 97 ns (KB), which is the L2 miss queue depth to look for.
DRAM fills enter the L2 as well as the L1 (inclusive, settled); the SLC takes only L2 victims (settled), so a streaming read through 12 MiB writes the SLC at the L2 eviction rate.
Consequence (mine): with the SLC exclusive, one core sweeping a buffer up to about 20 MiB (12 L2 + 8 SLC) still hits on chip; past that, both thrash together and latency jumps to DRAM.
